metadata.title: Supersaturation in Posets and Applications Involving the Container Method
metadata.authors: Jonathan A. Noel, Alex Scott, Benny Sudakov

nodes.name: Comparable pairs $\comp(S)$
nodes.statement: For a subset $S$ of a poset $P$, $\comp(S)$ denotes the number of comparable pairs in $S$.

nodes.name: Subspace poset $\Vectors{q}{n}$ and $q$-binomial coefficient
nodes.statement: Given prime power $q$ and $n\geq 1$, $\Vectors{q}{n}$ is the poset of all subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ ordered by inclusion. The $q$-binomial $\qbinom{n}{i}{q}$ counts subspaces of dimension $i$.

nodes.name: Multiset poset $\{0,1,2\}^n$ and rank counts $\ell_i(n)$
nodes.statement: On $\{0,1,2\}^n$, $x \leq y$ iff $x_j \leq y_j$ for all $j$. For $0\leq i\leq 2n$, $\ell_i(n)$ is the number of vectors whose coordinates sum to $i$.

nodes.name: $p$-random subset
nodes.statement: A $p$-random subset of $X$ includes each element of $X$ independently with probability $p$.

nodes.name: Comparability digraph
nodes.statement: A digraph $D$ with $V(D)=P$ such that every arc $(x,y)$ has $x$ comparable to $y$ in $P$, and for every comparable pair exactly one of $(x,y),(y,x)$ is in $E(D)$.

nodes.name: Ranked poset
nodes.statement: A poset $P$ is ranked if it partitions into non-empty levels $L_0,\dots,L_N$ such that $x\in L_i$ and $x<y$ imply $y\in\bigcup_{j>i}L_j$, and $x<y$ with $x\in L_i,y\in L_j$, $j>i+1$ implies some $z\in L_{i+1}$ with $x<z<y$.

nodes.name: Regular covering by chains
nodes.statement: A non-empty finite multiset $\mathscr{C}$ of maximal chains in a ranked poset $P$ such that every $x\in L_i$ is contained in exactly $|\mathscr{C}|/|L_i|$ chains of $\mathscr{C}$.

nodes.name: LYM property
nodes.statement: Ranked poset $P$ has the LYM property if for every antichain $A\subseteq P$, $\sum_{i=0}^N |A\cap L_i|/|L_i| \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Normalised matching property
nodes.statement: Ranked poset has normalised matching if for $0\leq i\leq N-1$ and $T\subseteq L_i$: $|\{y\in L_{i+1}: y>x \text{ for some } x\in T\}|/|L_{i+1}| \geq |T|/|L_i|$.

nodes.name: Fixed-2-count level slices $L_i^s$, $L_i^{\geq s}$, $L_i^{\leq s}$
nodes.statement: $L_i^s$ is the set of elements of $L_i$ with exactly $s$ coordinates equal to $2$. $L_i^{\geq s} := \bigcup_{r=s}^{\lfloor i/2\rfloor} L_i^r$ and $L_i^{\leq s} := \bigcup_{r=\max\{0,i-n\}}^{s} L_i^r$.

nodes.name: Memoryless distribution on chains
nodes.statement: A distribution $\mu$ on chains is memoryless if for $z_1<\dots<z_q$: $\mathbb{P}(z_q\in\mathcal{C}_\mu \mid z_1,\dots,z_{q-1}\in\mathcal{C}_\mu) = \mathbb{P}(z_q\in\mathcal{C}_\mu \mid z_{q-1}\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)$.

nodes.name: Container
nodes.statement: Given a collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $P$ such that every antichain is contained in some member of $\mathcal{F}$, the elements of $\mathcal{F}$ are called containers.

nodes.name: Bounded-cardinality subset family $\binom{X}{\leq j}$
nodes.statement: $\binom{X}{\leq j}$ denotes the set of all subsets of $X$ of cardinality at most $j$; for $n\geq j$, $\binom{n}{\leq j} := \sum_{r=0}^j \binom{n}{r}$.

nodes.name: Log-concave sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $a_0,\dots,a_N$ is log-concave if $a_{i+1}/a_i \leq a_i/a_{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq N-1$.

nodes.name: Sperner's Theorem
nodes.statement: The largest antichain in the boolean lattice $\mathcal{P}(n)$ has size $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.
conclusions: Largest antichain in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ has cardinality $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.

nodes.name: Kleitman's supersaturation in $\mathcal{P}(n)$
nodes.statement: For $1\leq m\leq 2^n$, $\comp$ in a subset of $\mathcal{P}(n)$ of size $m$ is minimised by collections whose cardinalities are as close to $n/2$ as possible.
conclusions: $\comp$ is minimised by sets of cardinalities concentrated near $n/2$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation in $\Vectors{q}{n}$ (Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq n_0(k)$, if $S\subseteq\Vectors{q}{n}$ has $|S|\geq \sum_{r=0}^{k-1}\qbinom{n}{\lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil}{q}+t$, then $\comp(S)\geq t\qbinom{\lceil(n+k)/2\rceil}{k}{q}$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation in $\{0,1,2\}^n$ (Theorem 1.4)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq n_0(k)$, if $S\subseteq\{0,1,2\}^n$ has $|S|\geq \sum_{r=n-\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}^{n+\lceil(k-1)/2\rceil}\ell_r(n)+t$, then $\comp(S)\geq (\ell_{3k-1}(n)/\ell_{2k-1}(n)-1)t$.

nodes.name: Counting antichains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$ (Theorem 1.5)
nodes.statement: For fixed prime power $q$, the number of antichains in $\mathcal{V}(q,n)$ is $2^{(1+O(\sqrt{n}q^{-n/4}))\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q}}$.

nodes.name: Counting antichains in $\{0,1,2\}^n$ (Theorem 1.6)
nodes.statement: The number of antichains in $\{0,1,2\}^n$ is $2^{(1+O(\sqrt{\log n/n}))\ell_n(n)}$.

nodes.name: Random antichains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$ (Theorem 1.7)
nodes.statement: There exists $c(\varepsilon,q)>0$ such that if $p\geq c(\varepsilon,q)/q^{n/2}$, then with high probability every antichain in a $p$-random subset of $\Vectors{q}{n}$ has cardinality at most $(1+\varepsilon)p\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q}$.
conclusions: w.h.p. every antichain in $p$-random subset has size $\leq (1+\varepsilon)p\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q}$

nodes.name: Random antichains in $\{0,1,2\}^n$ (Theorem 1.8)
nodes.statement: There exists $c(\varepsilon)>0$ such that if $p\geq c(\varepsilon)/n$, then with high probability every antichain in a $p$-random subset of $\{0,1,2\}^n$ has cardinality at most $(1+\varepsilon)p\ell_n(n)$.
conclusions: w.h.p. every antichain in $p$-random subset has size $\leq (1+\varepsilon)p\ell_n(n)$

nodes.name: Approximate Kleitman in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ (Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq n_0(k)$, if $S\subseteq \mathcal{P}(n)$ has $|S|\geq \sum_{r=0}^{k-1}\binom{n}{\lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil}+t$, then $\comp(S)\geq t\binom{\lceil(n+k)/2\rceil}{k}$.

nodes.name: Kleitman's equivalence (Theorem 4.5)
nodes.statement: For a ranked poset $P$, the following are equivalent: (1) $P$ has a regular covering by chains, (2) $P$ has the LYM property, (3) $P$ has the normalised matching property.
conclusions: (1) regular covering by chains $\iff$ (2) LYM property $\iff$ (3) normalised matching property

nodes.name: Counting antichains in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ (Theorem 6.1)
nodes.statement: The number of antichains in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ is at most $2^{(1+O(\sqrt{\log(n)/n}))\binom{n}{\lceil n/2\rceil}}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff Bound (Theorem 6.4)
nodes.statement: For independent $X_1,\dots,X_n\in\{0,1\}$ and $X=\sum X_i$: $\mathbb{P}(X>(1+\delta)\mathbb{E}(X))\leq e^{-\delta^2\mathbb{E}(X)/3}$ if $0<\delta<1$, $\leq e^{-\delta\mathbb{E}(X)/3}$ if $\delta>1$.

nodes.name: Wilf's asymptotics for $\Vectors{q}{n}$ (Theorem A.1)
nodes.statement: For fixed prime power $q$ and $n\to\infty$: $|\Vectors{q}{n}|=\Theta(q^{n^2/2})$ and $\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q}=\Theta(q^{n^2/2})$; in particular $|\Vectors{q}{n}|=\Theta(\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q})$.

nodes.name: Anderson's asymptotic for $\ell_n(n)$ (Theorem A.2)
nodes.statement: $\ell_n(n)=\Theta(3^n/\sqrt{n})$.

nodes.name: Log-concavity of $\ell_i(n)$ (Theorem A.3)
nodes.statement: The sequence $\ell_0(n),\dots,\ell_{2n}(n)$ is log-concave.

nodes.name: Hall's Marriage Theorem
nodes.statement: A bipartite graph admits a perfect matching from one side iff Hall's condition holds: every subset $T$ has $|N(T)|\geq |T|$.
conclusions: matching saturating $A$ exists iff $|N(T)|\geq |T|$ for all $T\subseteq A$

nodes.name: Random-chain comparable-pair lower bound (Lemma 2.2)
nodes.statement: $\comp(S)\geq \left(\max_{(x,y)\in E(D)}\mathbb{P}(y\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)\right)^{-1}\left(|S|-\left(\min_{x\in P}\mathbb{P}(x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)\right)^{-1}\right)$.

nodes.name: Conditional probability bound under $\mu$ (Lemma 4.10)
nodes.statement: Under the constructed memoryless distribution $\mu$ on chains of $\{0,1,2\}^n$, if $|i-j|\geq k$, $\min\{i,j\}\geq 2k$ or $\max\{i,j\}\leq 2n-2k$, $|j-n|\leq |i-n|$, and $x\in L_i,y\in L_j$ comparable, then $\mathbb{P}(y\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)\leq (\ell_{3k-1}(n)/\ell_{2k-1}(n)-1)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Single-step container lemma (Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: If $|P|>m$ and every $S\subseteq P$ with $|S|>m$ has $\comp(S)\geq |S|d$, then there exists $f:\binom{P}{\leq |P|/(2d+1)}\to\binom{P}{\leq m}$ such that every antichain $I\subseteq P$ has $T\subseteq I$ with $|T|\leq |P|/(2d+1)$, $T\cap f(T)=\emptyset$, $I\subseteq T\cup f(T)$.
conclusions: existence of container function $f$ with stated properties

nodes.name: Multi-stage container lemma (Lemma 5.3)
nodes.statement: Given $d_1>\dots>d_k$ and $m_0>\dots>m_k$ with $|P|=m_0$ and $\comp(S)\geq |S|d_j$ when $|S|>m_j$, there exist functions $f_1,\dots,f_k$ with $f_j:\binom{P}{\leq \sum_{r=1}^j m_{r-1}/(2d_r+1)}\to\binom{P}{\leq m_j}$ and disjoint $T_1,\dots,T_k\subseteq I$ satisfying conditions (i)-(iv).

nodes.name: Container collection $\mathcal{F}$ (Lemma 5.4)
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 5.3, there is a collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $P$ with (a) $|\mathcal{F}|\leq \prod_{r=1}^k \binom{m_{r-1}}{\leq m_{r-1}/(2d_r+1)}$, (b) $|A|\leq m_k+\sum_{r=1}^k m_{r-1}/(2d_r+1)$ for $A\in\mathcal{F}$, (c) every antichain $I\subseteq A$ for some $A\in\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\ell_{i+1}(n)/\ell_i(n)$, $1\leq i\leq n-3$ (Lemma A.4)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 4$ and $1\leq i\leq n-3$: $\frac{n+1}{i+1}\leq \frac{\ell_{i+1}(n)}{\ell_i(n)}\leq \frac{\lceil i/2\rceil-\lfloor i/2\rfloor}{\lceil i/2\rceil}+\frac{n-\lceil i/2\rceil}{\lceil(i+2)/2\rceil}$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\ell_{n-1}(n)/\ell_{n-2}(n)$ (Lemma A.5)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 5$: $\frac{n+2}{n}\leq \frac{\ell_{n-1}(n)}{\ell_{n-2}(n)}\leq \frac{4n+7}{4n-2}$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\ell_n(n)/\ell_{n-1}(n)$ (Lemma A.6)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 5$: $\frac{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil-\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil}+\frac{\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor}{\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil}\leq \frac{\ell_n(n)}{\ell_{n-1}(n)}\leq \frac{n+1}{n}$.

nodes.name: Weight comparison $w_{i,s}'<w_{i,s}$ (Proposition 4.11)
nodes.statement: For $1\leq i\leq n-1$ and $0\leq s<i/2$, $w_{i,s}' < w_{i,s}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound $w_{i,s}\leq 2/((i+1)|L_{i+1}|)$ (Proposition 4.12)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 5$, $1\leq i\leq n-1$, $0\leq s<i/2$: $w_{i,s}\leq \frac{2}{(i+1)|L_{i+1}|}$.

nodes.name: Single-step conditional probability (Corollary 4.13)
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 5$, $0\leq i\leq 2n-1$, $x\in L_i$, $y\in L_{i+1}$ with $x<y$: $\mathbb{P}(y\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)\leq 2|L_i|/((i+1)|L_{i+1}|)$ if $i\leq n-1$, else $\leq 2/(2n-i)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2 generalises to general graphs
nodes.statement: The proof of Lemma 2.2 generalises to give a lower bound on the number of edges induced by a set of $m$ vertices in a general graph $G$, by orienting edges and selecting a random clique under $\mu$.

nodes.name: Comparison with Balogh-Treglown-Wagner and Korshunov
nodes.statement: BTW used a single-stage container lemma yielding weaker bounds; Korshunov obtained precise asymptotics for the number of antichains in $\mathcal{P}(n)$. Choosing $k>2$ in Lemma 5.3 does not improve the proven bounds.

nodes.name: Constant-factor supersaturation suffices
nodes.statement: Container-method applications typically only need supersaturation results best possible up to a constant factor (e.g. Erdos-Simonovits).

nodes.name: Middle-levels conjecture for $\{0,\dots,r\}^n$ (Conjecture 7.1)
nodes.statement: For $n$ large w.r.t. $r$ and $1\leq m\leq (r+1)^n$, the number of comparable pairs in a subset of $\{0,\dots,r\}^n$ of cardinality $m$ is minimised by a set whose elements have coordinate sum as close to $rn/2$ as possible.

nodes.name: Weak form of middle-levels conjecture (Conjecture 7.2)
nodes.statement: For positive integers $r,k$ there exists $c(r,k)>0$ such that for every $S\subseteq\{0,\dots,r\}^n$, $\comp(S)\geq (|S|-k\ell_{\lceil rn/2\rceil}(n,r))c(r,k)n^k$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation for general divisor posets
nodes.statement: Prove a non-trivial supersaturation theorem for the poset of divisors of a general integer (perhaps with the number of distinct prime factors large w.r.t. the largest multiplicity).

nodes.name: Supersaturation for non-ranked / non-LYM posets
nodes.statement: Prove supersaturation results for posets without regular coverings by chains, or for posets which are not even ranked.

nodes.name: Improving antichain-counting bounds
nodes.statement: Improve the bounds on the number of antichains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$ and $\{0,1,2\}^n$ (Theorems 1.5 and 1.6) and obtain similar bounds for other posets.

nodes.name: $\ell_i(n)$ closed form (Eq. 1.1)
nodes.statement: $\ell_i(n)=\sum_{s=\max\{0,i-n\}}^{\lfloor i/2\rfloor}\binom{n}{i-s}\binom{i-s}{s}$.

nodes.name: Weight $w_{i,s}$ (Eq. 4.4)
nodes.statement: $w_{i,s}=\frac{|L_i||L_{i+1}^{\geq s+1}|-|L_{i+1}||L_i^{\geq s+1}|}{|L_i^s||L_i||L_{i+1}|(i-2s)}$ for $\max\{0,i-n\}\leq s\leq \lfloor(i-1)/2\rfloor$.

nodes.name: Weight $w_{i,s}'$ (Eq. 4.5)
nodes.statement: $w_{i,s}'=\frac{|L_i||L_{i+1}^{\leq s}|-|L_{i+1}||L_i^{\leq s-1}|}{|L_i^s||L_i||L_{i+1}|(n-i+s)}$ for $\max\{0,i-n+1\}\leq s\leq \lfloor i/2\rfloor$.

nodes.name: $1\to 2$ Coordinate Claim (Claim 4.16)
nodes.statement: If $\exists \alpha\in[n]$ with $x_\alpha=0$ and $y_\alpha=2$, then for every $\beta\in[n]$ with $x_\beta=1$, $y_\beta=2$.

nodes.name: Construction of memoryless distribution $\mu$ on chains of $\{0,1,2\}^n$
nodes.statement: Iteratively builds a maximal chain $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ in $\{0,1,2\}^n$ level by level using weights $w_{i,s},w_{i,s}'$ so that $\mu$ is memoryless and each level element is chosen with uniform marginal.
output: Distribution $\mu$ satisfying memorylessness and uniform per-level marginals

nodes.name: Kleitman-Winston container algorithm
nodes.statement: Greedy peeling of high-degree elements from the comparability graph; outputs sets $T_1,\dots,T_k$ and containers $f_j(\bigcup T_r)$ used to cover any antichain.
output: Container values $f_j(\bigcup_{r=1}^j T_r)\subseteq P$ with $|f_j(\cdot)|\leq m_j$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Induction on $|S|$; either find a vertex of high $D$-out-degree in $S$ and reduce, or use $k-\binom{k}{2}\leq 1$ on $|\mathcal{C}_\mu\cap S|$ to bound the sum.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1 (approximate Kleitman)
nodes.statement: Split $\mathcal{P}(n)$ into mod-$k$ residue posets $P_r$, induct on $t_r$, shift small sets up using a Hall-style greedy step, then apply Lemma 2.2 to a uniformly random maximal chain of $P_r^*$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2 (subspace supersaturation)
nodes.statement: Same scheme as Theorem 3.1 but with subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ split by rank mod $k$ and uniform random maximal chains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4 assuming Lemma 4.10
nodes.statement: Split $\{0,1,2\}^n$ into mod-$k$ residue posets, induct on $t_r$, use Hall + log-concavity to remove low-rank elements, apply Lemmas 2.2 and 4.10.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.10 (conditional probability)
nodes.statement: Three cases by gap $j-i$ and parity of $i+j$: small gap via product of single-step bounds; symmetric large gap via coordinate-swap maximality; asymmetric large gap by induction.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.11
nodes.statement: Compare two weight redistribution schemes on $L_i\to L_{i+1}$ and use monotonicity of $f(s)=s/(n+1-s)+(i+1-2s)/(n-s)$ in $s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.12
nodes.statement: Cases on $s$ relative to a threshold $s_0$ defined by inequality (4.6); base case $s=0$ via a simple comparable-pair count, then bidirectional induction (on $s$ for $s\leq s_0$, on $\lfloor i/2\rfloor-s$ for $s>s_0$).

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.13
nodes.statement: Direct from Propositions 4.11 and 4.12 plus boundary case at $s=i/2$ using Lemmas A.4-A.6, with the upper-half case derived by symmetry equations $(\ref{sym1}),(\ref{sym2})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3 (multi-stage container)
nodes.statement: Apply the Kleitman-Winston peeling algorithm with thresholds $2d_1>\dots>2d_k$; verify well-definedness of $f_j$ by induction on the algorithm's history.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: Direct construction: take $\mathcal{F}=\{(\bigcup T_{r,I})\cup f_k(\bigcup T_{r,I}) : I \text{ antichain}\}$ and bound the count by enumerating choices of each $T_{j,I}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1 (counting antichains in $\mathcal{P}(n)$)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.4 with $k=2$, $d_1=n\sqrt{\log n}$, $d_2=\sqrt{n\log n}$, then sum over containers and apply Stirling.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.5 (counting antichains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$)
nodes.statement: Same scheme as Theorem 6.1 but with $k=1$, $d=\sqrt{n}q^{n/4}$, using Wilf's bounds on $|\Vectors{q}{n}|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.6 (counting antichains in $\{0,1,2\}^n$)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.4 with $k=2$, $d_1=n\sqrt{\log n}$, $d_2=\sqrt{n\log n}$ and Anderson's $\ell_n(n)=\Theta(3^n/\sqrt{n})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.7 (random antichains in $\Vectors{q}{n}$)
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 5.2 to obtain containers, bound the probability of a large antichain in $A_p$ by Chernoff applied to each container, then union bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.8 (random antichains in $\{0,1,2\}^n$)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.3 with $k=2$, $d_1=n^2/200$, $d_2=\varepsilon n/12$, then Chernoff + union bound over $T_1,T_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.4
nodes.statement: Weight-redistribution: assign weight 1 to each $y\in L_{i+1}$, push down to comparable $x\in L_i$, and observe $f(s)=(i-2s)/(i-s)+(n-i+s)/(i-s+1)$ is monotone in $s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.5
nodes.statement: Same redistribution with $i=n-2$; $f(s)$ is non-decreasing for $s\leq (n-5)/3$, then non-increasing, giving the stated two-sided bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.6
nodes.statement: Same redistribution with $i=n-1$; $f(s)$ is decreasing on $0\leq s\leq \lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 4.16
nodes.statement: Suppose $\exists\beta$ with $x_\beta=y_\beta=1$; define swap $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}$ and an injection $\pi$ on chains; show $\mathbb{P}(\tau(y)\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x)>\mathbb{P}(y\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x)$, contradicting maximality.

nodes.name: Inductive base case for $|S|$
nodes.statement: Base case $|S|\leq (\min_{x\in P}\mathbb{P}(x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu))^{-1}$: bound is trivial.

nodes.name: Reduce by high-out-degree element
nodes.statement: If some $w\in S$ has $d_S^+(w)\geq (\max_{(x,y)\in E(D)}\mathbb{P}(y\mid x))^{-1}$, apply IH to $S\setminus\{w\}$ and add the $\geq d_S^+(w)$ pairs through $w$.

nodes.name: Bound via $k-\binom{k}{2}\leq 1$
nodes.statement: Otherwise every $w\in S$ has $d_S^+(w)<(\max\mathbb{P}(y\mid x))^{-1}$; apply $k-\binom{k}{2}\leq 1$ to $|\mathcal{C}_\mu\cap S|$ and rearrange.

nodes.name: Conclude lower bound on $\comp(S)$
nodes.statement: Plug in lower bound on $\mathbb{P}(w\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)$ and rearrange to derive the stated bound on $\comp(S)=\sum_w d_S^+(w)$.

nodes.name: Partition $\mathcal{P}(n)$ by rank mod $k$
nodes.statement: Define $P_r$ to be subsets whose cardinality is $\equiv \lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil \bmod k$ and $S_r=S\cap P_r$, $t_r=|S_r|-\binom{n}{\lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil}$.

nodes.name: Inductive setup on $t_r$
nodes.statement: Induct on $t_r$. If $S_r$ contains $x$ comparable to $\geq \binom{\lceil(n+k)/2\rceil}{k}$ elements of $S_r$, apply IH to $S_r\setminus\{x\}$.

nodes.name: Shift away small sets via greedy matching
nodes.statement: For each small set $x\in X$ pick a distinct $y_x\in P_r\setminus S_r$ of size $k+s$ with $x<y_x$; replace $X$ by $\{y_x\}$ to assume $X=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Define digraph $D$ on $P_r^*$
nodes.statement: Orient each comparable pair so the head's cardinality is closer to $n/2$, with a tie-break for $|x|=n-|y|$.

nodes.name: Apply uniform random maximal chain
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ = uniform maximal chain in $\mathcal{P}(n)$ intersected with $P_r^*$; verify $\mathbb{P}(x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)\geq \binom{n}{\lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil}^{-1}$ and $\mathbb{P}(y\mid x)\leq \binom{\lceil(n+k)/2\rceil}{k}^{-1}$, then apply Lemma 2.2.

nodes.name: Partition $\Vectors{q}{n}$ by rank mod $k$
nodes.statement: Define $P_r$ = subspaces of dimension $\equiv \lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil \bmod k$ and $S_r=S\cap P_r$, $t_r=|S_r|-\qbinom{n}{\lceil(n-k+1+2r)/2\rceil}{q}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $S_r$ of dimension $\geq k$
nodes.statement: Shift up small-dimension elements of $S_r$ as in the boolean case; uses $\qbinom{n-k+1}{k}{q}-\qbinom{\lceil(n+k)/2\rceil}{k}{q}\geq \qbinom{n}{k-1}{q}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.2 with random maximal chain
nodes.statement: Take $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ = uniform maximal chain in $\Vectors{q}{n}$ intersected with $P_r^*$; verify the two probability bounds and conclude.

nodes.name: Partition $\{0,1,2\}^n$ by rank mod $k$
nodes.statement: Define $P_r$ = elements of rank $\equiv n+\lceil(2r-k+1)/2\rceil \bmod k$ and $t_r=|S_r|-\ell_{n+\lceil(2r-k+1)/2\rceil}(n)$.

nodes.name: Inductive comparability assumption
nodes.statement: Assume every element of $S_r$ has $<\ell_{3k-1}(n)/\ell_{2k-1}(n)-1$ comparable elements in $S_r$.

nodes.name: Hall + log-concavity to drop ranks $<2k$
nodes.statement: If $|\Gamma(T)\setminus S_r|<|T|$ for some $T\subseteq A$, normalised matching plus log-concavity (Theorem A.3) gives a comparable element exceeding the threshold; hence $S_r$ has no rank-$<2k$ elements.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 2.2 and 4.10 on $P_r^*$
nodes.statement: Define $D$ on $P_r^*$ orienting toward rank closer to $n$; apply $\mu$ to get the conditional bound from Lemma 4.10 and conclude via Lemma 2.2.

nodes.name: Reduction by symmetry to $i<n$
nodes.statement: By symmetry $(\ref{sym1}),(\ref{sym2})$ of $\mu$ around level $n$, may assume $i<n$, hence $i<j$ and $i+j\leq 2n$.

nodes.name: Case 4.14 small gap $k\leq j-i\leq 11n/10$
nodes.statement: Sum over chains $z_i<\dots<z_j$, use memorylessness and Corollary 4.13, bound $(j-i)!\cdot\prod \mathbb{P}(z_{r+1}\mid z_r)$ by $2^{j-i}(j-i)!(n-\lfloor(j-i)/2\rfloor)!/(n^{\lceil(j-i)/2\rceil}n!)$, apply Stirling.

nodes.name: Case 4.15 symmetric large gap $i+j=2n$, $i<9n/20$
nodes.statement: Choose $(x,y)$ to maximise $\mathbb{P}(y\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x\in\mathcal{C}_\mu)$. Use Claim 4.16 to deduce $y_\beta=2$ for all $\beta$ with $x_\beta\geq 1$; count $\geq \binom{\lceil 11n/20\rceil}{k}$ valid $y'$ giving same conditional probability; conclude via $\sum\mathbb{P}\leq 1$.

nodes.name: Case 4.17 asymmetric large gap by induction on $2n-i-j$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\mathbb{P}(y\mid x)=\sum_z \mathbb{P}(z\mid x)\mathbb{P}(y\mid z)$ via memorylessness; apply small-gap or symmetric-gap case at each $z\in L_{i+1}$ or recurse using IH.

nodes.name: Two redistribution rules
nodes.statement: Define rule R1 using $w_{i,s},w_{i,s}'$ and rule R2 distributing weight evenly to comparable elements; under R2 each $y\in L_{i+1}^s$ receives $f(s)=s/(n+1-s)+(i+1-2s)/(n-s)$.

nodes.name: Show $f(s)$ strictly decreasing in $s$
nodes.statement: Compute $f(s+1)-f(s)$ and show numerator negative for $0\leq s\leq (i-1)/2$ in cases $i\in\{n-2,n-1\}$ and $1\leq i\leq n-3$.

nodes.name: Compare R1 and R2 to conclude $w_{i,s}'<w_{i,s}$
nodes.statement: R1 sends equal weight to each element of $L_{i+1}$; R2 sends more weight to elements with fewer 2-coordinates. Therefore each $x\in L_i^s$ under R1 sends more to $L_{i+1}^{s+1}$ than to $L_{i+1}^s$.

nodes.name: Define threshold $s_0$
nodes.statement: Let $s_0$ be the largest $s$ for which inequality (4.6) holds, else $s_0=0$. Use monotonicity of both sides in $s$.

nodes.name: Base case $s=0$
nodes.statement: Reduce target inequality to $(i+1)|L_{i+1}|\leq (n+i)|L_i|$; prove by counting comparable pairs as $\sum (i+1-r)|L_{i+1}^r|=\sum(n-r)|L_i^r|$ and rearranging.

nodes.name: Case $1\leq s\leq s_0$: induct on $s$
nodes.statement: Subtract IH inequality from target; reduces (after substitution) to inequality (4.6) which holds because $s\leq s_0$.

nodes.name: Case $s_0<s<i/2$: induct on $\lfloor i/2\rfloor-s$
nodes.statement: Boundary cases $s=(i-1)/2,(i-2)/2$ direct; otherwise IH at $s+1$ plus the negation of (4.6) at $s+1$ (since $s+1>s_0$) implies the bound at $s$.

nodes.name: Sub-case $i\leq n-1$
nodes.statement: If $s<i/2$, both $w_{i,s},w_{i,s}'$ are bounded by $2/((i+1)|L_{i+1}|)$ via Propositions 4.11, 4.12. If $s=i/2$ then $w_{i,i/2}=0$ and $w_{i,i/2}'=2/(2n-i)$, bounded via Lemmas A.4-A.6.

nodes.name: Sub-case $i\geq n$ via symmetry
nodes.statement: Use $(\ref{sym1}),(\ref{sym2})$ together with $\mathbb{P}(y\mid x)=\mathbb{P}(x\mid y)|L_{i+1}|/|L_i|$ to reduce to the previous sub-case.

nodes.name: Algorithm correctness setup
nodes.statement: Run Kleitman-Winston peeling: degrees $d_{P_i}(u_i)$ are non-increasing, so each $T_j,f_j$ is finalised at a unique step.

nodes.name: Verify (i)-(iv)
nodes.statement: Properties (CONTSinf), (CONTdisjoint), (CONTcontainersContain), (CONTeachSSmall) follow from algorithm construction and the supersaturation hypothesis $\comp(\cdot)\geq |\cdot|d_j$.

nodes.name: Well-definedness of $f_j$
nodes.statement: If two antichains $I,I'$ yield the same $\bigcup T_r$, induct on step index to show $u_t=u_t',P_t=P_t'$; hence $f_j(\bigcup T_r)$ depends only on $\bigcup T_r$.

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{F}$ from antichains
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}=\{(\bigcup_r T_{r,I})\cup f_k(\bigcup_r T_{r,I}) : I\text{ antichain}\}$; (b),(c) immediate.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}|$ by counting choices
nodes.statement: Number of $T_{1,I}$ choices is $\leq \binom{|P|}{\leq |P|/(2d_1+1)}$; for $j\geq 2$, $T_{j,I}\subseteq f_{j-1}(\bigcup_{r<j}T_{r,I})$ gives $\leq \binom{m_{j-1}}{\leq m_{j-1}/(2d_j+1)}$ choices.

nodes.name: Choose parameters $d_1,d_2,m_0,m_1,m_2$
nodes.statement: Set $d_1=n\sqrt{\log n}$, $d_2=\sqrt{n\log n}$, $m_0=2^n$, $m_1=2\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}/(1-8d_1/n^2)$, $m_2=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}/(1-2d_2/n)$.

nodes.name: Check supersaturation thresholds
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 3.1 to verify $\comp(S)\geq |S|d_j$ for $|S|\geq m_j$, $j=1,2$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.4 and bound exponent
nodes.statement: Bound number of antichains by $\binom{2^n}{\leq 2^n/d_1}\binom{m_1}{\leq m_1/d_2}2^{m_2+m_1/d_2+2^n/d_1}$ and simplify exponent via Stirling to $(1+O(\sqrt{\log n/n}))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$.

nodes.name: Choose parameters in $\Vectors{q}{n}$
nodes.statement: Set $d=\sqrt{n}q^{n/4}$, $m=\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q}/(1-d\qbinom{\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil}{1}{q}^{-1})$; $m,N=\Theta(q^{n^2/2})$ by Wilf.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.4 with $k=1$
nodes.statement: Bound $\#\text{antichains}\leq \binom{N}{\leq N/d}2^{m+N/d}$, simplify via $N=\Theta(\qbinom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}{q})$ and $\qbinom{\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil}{1}{q}=\Theta(q^{n/2})$.

nodes.name: Verify supersaturation via Theorem 1.4
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 1.4 to obtain $\comp(S)\geq |S|d_j$ at each threshold.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.4 and Anderson
nodes.statement: Use Theorem A.2 ($\ell_n(n)=\Theta(3^n/\sqrt{n})$) to simplify $m_2+O((3^n\log n)/d_1+(m_1\log n)/d_2)$ to $(1+O(\sqrt{\log n/n}))\ell_n(n)$.

nodes.name: Set parameters and apply Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Take $m=(1+\varepsilon/2)\qbinom{n}{\lceil n/2\rceil}{q}$, $d=(\varepsilon/3)\qbinom{\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil}{1}{q}$; obtain container function $f$.

nodes.name: Bound bad event via Chernoff
nodes.statement: For each $T\subseteq\Vectors{q}{n}$ with $|T|\leq N/(2d+1)$, bound $\mathbb{P}(T\subseteq A_p)\cdot\mathbb{P}(|A_p\cap f(T)|\geq p(1+\varepsilon)\qbinom{n}{\lceil n/2\rceil}{q}-|T|)$ via Theorem 6.4.

nodes.name: Union bound over containers
nodes.statement: Sum $\binom{N}{a}p^a$ over $a\leq N/(2d+1)$, choose $c(\varepsilon,q)$ large enough so log-term is $<\varepsilon^2 mp/200$; get $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Set parameters $d_1,d_2,m_1,m_2$
nodes.statement: $m_1=3\ell_n(n)$, $m_2=(1+\varepsilon/2)\ell_n(n)$, $d_1=n^2/200$, $d_2=\varepsilon n/12$.

nodes.name: Apply multi-stage container Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: Obtain $f_1,f_2$; for fixed $T_1,T_2$, bound $\mathbb{P}(T_1\cup T_2\subseteq A_p)\cdot\mathbb{P}(|A_p\cap f_2(\cdot)|\geq p(1+\varepsilon)\ell_n(n)-|T_1\cup T_2|)$ via Chernoff.

nodes.name: Sum and choose $c(\varepsilon)$ large
nodes.statement: Double sum over $T_1,T_2$ bounded above by $\left(\frac{3^n}{2d_1+1}\right)\left(\frac{m_1}{2d_2+1}\right)(3ed_1p)^{3^n/(2d_1+1)}(3ed_2p)^{m_1/(2d_2+1)}e^{-\varepsilon^2\ell_n(n)p/100}$, choose $c(\varepsilon)$ large to get $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Setup swap $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}$
nodes.statement: Assume $x_\beta=y_\beta=1$; introduce coordinate-swap $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}$ and observe $x<\tau_{\alpha,\beta}(y)$.

nodes.name: Construct injection $\pi$ on chains
nodes.statement: For each chain $Z=(z_i,\dots,z_{2n-i})$ from $x$ to $y$, define $\ell(Z)$ = first index with $z_\ell$'s $\alpha$-coordinate equal to 2 and $\pi(Z)$ swapping all later entries; $\pi$ is injective.

nodes.name: Probability invariance under $\pi$
nodes.statement: By the construction of $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ via $w_{i,s},w_{i,s}'$ which only depend on the 2-count, $\mathbb{P}(z_{i+1},\dots\in\mathcal{C}_\mu\mid x)=\mathbb{P}(\pi(Z))$.

nodes.name: Strict inequality from extra chain
nodes.statement: Exhibit a chain $x<z<\tau_{\alpha,\beta}(y)$ with $z_\beta=2$ not in image of $\pi$, giving strict inequality and contradicting maximality of $(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Initialise $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ at level 0 and 1
nodes.statement: Add $(0,\dots,0)$ to $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ with probability 1; add a uniformly random element of $L_1$.

nodes.name: Iterate: extend chain to level $i+1$
nodes.statement: For $1\leq i\leq 2n-2$: given $\mathcal{C}_\mu\cap L_i=\{x\}$ with $x\in L_i^s$, add $y\in L_{i+1}^{s+1}$ comparable to $x$ with probability $|L_i|w_{i,s}$, or $y\in L_{i+1}^s$ with probability $|L_i|w_{i,s}'$, independent of previous levels.

nodes.name: Terminate at $(2,\dots,2)$
nodes.statement: Add $(2,\dots,2)$ to $\mathcal{C}_\mu$ with probability one.

nodes.name: Initialise $P_0=P$, choose maximum-degree vertex $u_0$
nodes.statement: Set $P_0:=P$; let $u_0\in P_0$ maximise $d_{P_0}(\cdot)$, ties broken by total order.

nodes.name: Big-degree case: $d_{P_{i-1}}(u_{i-1})\geq 2d_k$
nodes.statement: Let $j$ = smallest index with $d_{P_{i-1}}(u_{i-1})\geq 2d_j$. If $u_{i-1}\in I$, add to $T_j$ and remove $\{u_{i-1}\}\cup N_{P_{i-1}}(u_{i-1})$; else just remove $u_{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Threshold drop: finalise $T_{j+\ell}$ and $f_{j+\ell}$
nodes.statement: If $P_i=\emptyset$ or $d_{P_i}(u_i)<2d_j$, find largest $\ell$ with $d_{P_i}(u_i)<2d_{j+\ell}$; set $T_{j+1}=\dots=T_{j+\ell}=\emptyset$ and $f_j(\bigcup T_r)=\dots=f_{j+\ell}(\bigcup T_r):=P_i$.

nodes.name: Small-degree termination
nodes.statement: If $d_{P_{i-1}}(u_{i-1})<2d_k$, terminate the algorithm.
